task_1.title: Stop forcing CMake try-compile configuration in CMakeToolchain
task_1.description: Version 2.19.1 hotfixes Conan's CMake integration so generated toolchains no longer automatically define CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION. This avoids MSVC configuration failures in projects that rely on legacy CMake try-compile checks such as check_function_exists(), while leaving try-compile configuration under CMake or user control.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.19.1 stops CMakeToolchain from forcing a try-compile configuration so MSVC projects using legacy CMake probe logic continue to configure correctly.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeToolchain generates a toolchain, it should no longer automatically define CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION for standard build types. Conan should stop injecting its own try-compile configuration so CMake try_compile-based checks, including legacy check_function_exists() flows under MSVC, run without the Conan-imposed configuration value. If a user supplies CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION separately, Conan should not replace it with an auto-generated value.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CMake toolchains should let try-compile checks use the normal CMake or user-provided configuration behavior instead of forcing Conan's selected build configuration. This should remove the MSVC compatibility issue seen in older CMake feature-detection logic.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to removing the automatic CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION definition from CMakeToolchain. It must not introduce a new required API, must not force an alternative try-compile value, and must preserve the ability for externally provided CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION values to remain effective.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should only relax Conan's control over try-compile configuration. It should not require consumers to adopt a new interface or replace the removed behavior with another forced default.

behavior: CMakeToolchain no longer emits an automatic CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION assignment based on the selected build type.

MSVC builds that execute legacy CMake try-compile checks, including check_function_exists(), are no longer subject to the Conan-generated try-compile configuration that triggered the reported failures.
Try-compile configuration remains governed by CMake defaults or by values explicitly supplied by the user rather than by Conan's generated toolchain.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer upgrades to 2.19.1 and generates a toolchain with CMakeToolchain, the generated toolchain should not automatically define CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION for standard configurations such as Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo, or MinSizeRel.
When a project configured with MSVC relies on legacy CMake probe logic built on try_compile, upgrading to 2.19.1 should avoid the failure mode caused by Conan forcing CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION.
When a consumer provides CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_CONFIGURATION explicitly outside Conan, upgrading to 2.19.1 should leave that externally supplied configuration in control.
